svg.title: Build a Sellable Delivery System in 30 Days
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-offer-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Build a Sellable Delivery System in 30 Days; subtitle: Four weekly milestones produce evidence, not an assumed first-month deal.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values are milestone-ending day numbers. The canonical time to first deal is 1–4 months; this sprint creates sales and delivery readiness without assuming signed revenue by day 30.; caption: Finish with one bounded offer, a tested reference workflow, a permissioned pilot plan, and a measured sales cohort. Continue discovery and runway management if the first contract has not closed.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one buyer, one workflow, and one acceptance test; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Interview five target operators, map the current workflow, and document measurable pain. Produce an offer sheet with explicit exclusions and an initial unit-cost worksheet; interview counts are targets, not evidence of demand by themselves.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build the reference workflow and a held-out test set; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Implement with synthetic data, define failure categories, and test retries, access boundaries, and rollback. Measure delivery hours and runtime costs so the fixed fee reflects actual effort.; label: Days 15-21; value: Package commercial terms and demonstrate bounded performance; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Prepare the statement of work, processing terms, access checklist, and support schedule. Demonstrate results against the held-out fixtures; use real client data only after the applicable access and processing requirements are satisfied.; label: Days 22-30; value: Run qualified sales conversations and rehearse the handoff; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Issue scoped proposals to qualified buyers and record objections by category. Rehearse intake, deployment, incident response, and retainer reporting. If no contract closes, continue the 1–4 month selling plan without booking hypothetical revenue.

text.title: Build a Sellable Delivery System in 30 Days
text.tspan: Build a Sellable Delivery System in 30 Days

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one buyer, one workflow, and one acceptance test; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Interview five target operators, map the current workflow, and document measurable pain. Produce an offer sheet with explicit exclusions and an initial unit-cost worksheet; interview counts are targets, not evidence of demand by themselves.

text.title: Choose one buyer, one workflow, and one acceptance test

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Build the reference workflow and a held-out test set; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Implement with synthetic data, define failure categories, and test retries, access boundaries, and rollback. Measure delivery hours and runtime costs so the fixed fee reflects actual effort.

text.title: Build the reference workflow and a held-out test set

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Package commercial terms and demonstrate bounded performance; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Prepare the statement of work, processing terms, access checklist, and support schedule. Demonstrate results against the held-out fixtures; use real client data only after the applicable access and processing requirements are satisfied.

text.title: Package commercial terms and demonstrate bounded performance

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Run qualified sales conversations and rehearse the handoff; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Issue scoped proposals to qualified buyers and record objections by category. Rehearse intake, deployment, incident response, and retainer reporting. If no contract closes, continue the 1–4 month selling plan without booking hypothetical revenue.

text.title: Run qualified sales conversations and rehearse the handoff
